shorts.title: Starbucks: How a Seattle Coffee Bean Shop Took Over the World
shorts.covers: Three friends selling beans in 1971, Howard Schultz's trip to Milan, the idea of the 'third place' between home and work, and the expansion that put a store on almost every high street.
shorts.subject: Starbucks
shorts.source: Starbucks official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Starbucks: From One Bean Shop to the World
script.description: In 1971 Starbucks sold coffee beans and never poured a single cup. Then a young salesman walked into an espresso bar in Milan, and saw a different business entirely.

shorts.title: Zara: The Shop That Makes Clothes in Weeks, Not Months
shorts.covers: Amancio Ortega making bathrobes in A Coruña, the first Zara store in 1975, the fast design-to-shelf system, and how Inditex became the world's biggest fashion retailer.
shorts.subject: Inditex Zara
shorts.source: Inditex Zara official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Zara: New Clothes in Weeks, Not Months
script.description: A shop boy who left school at fourteen built the world's biggest fashion business by doing one thing faster than anyone else: getting new clothes into shops in a few weeks.

shorts.title: Google: The Search Engine Built in a Garage
shorts.covers: Larry Page and Sergey Brin's PageRank research at Stanford, the garage office, the ad model that paid for free search, and the growth into Android, YouTube and Alphabet.
shorts.subject: Google
shorts.source: Google official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Google: The Search Engine Built in a Garage
script.description: Two students tried to sell their search engine for under a million dollars and were turned down. Then they rented a garage, and Google grew into one of the biggest companies in history.

shorts.title: Uber: The Taxi Company With No Taxis
shorts.covers: Garrett Camp and Travis Kalanick failing to find a cab in Paris, black cars on demand in San Francisco, rapid global expansion, fights with regulators and the leadership change that followed.
shorts.subject: Uber
shorts.source: Uber official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Uber: The Taxi Company With No Taxis
script.description: On a cold night in Paris, two young founders could not find a taxi. Their answer was an app that turned millions of ordinary cars into rides at the press of a button.

shorts.title: Ferrari: The Racing Team That Sells Cars to Pay for It
shorts.covers: Enzo Ferrari driving for Alfa Romeo, founding his own team, selling road cars to fund racing, the prancing horse badge, and the scarcity that keeps the brand so valuable.
shorts.subject: Ferrari
shorts.source: Ferrari official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Ferrari: The Racing Team That Sells Cars
script.description: Enzo Ferrari only wanted to win races. To pay for it, he started selling road cars to wealthy drivers, and turned scarcity into one of the most valuable brands in the world.

shorts.title: LEGO: The Toy Company That Almost Broke
shorts.covers: Ole Kirk Christiansen's wooden toys in Billund, the plastic brick of 1958, too many products and losses in the early 2000s, and the comeback built on films and licensed sets.
shorts.subject: LEGO
shorts.source: LEGO official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: LEGO: The Toy Company That Almost Broke
script.description: A Danish carpenter made wooden toys to survive the Great Depression. His family turned a plastic brick into the world's favourite toy, then nearly lost it all.

shorts.title: Rolex: The Watch Company Owned by a Charity
shorts.covers: Hans Wilsdorf founding a watch business in London in 1905, the waterproof Oyster, the move to Geneva, and why the company is owned by a foundation rather than shareholders.
shorts.subject: Rolex
shorts.source: Rolex official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Rolex: The Watch Company Owned by a Charity
script.description: A German orphan in London decided that people would one day wear their watches on their wrists. Rolex became the world's best-known watch, and today a charitable foundation owns it.

shorts.title: Nestlé: The Baby Food That Grew Into the World's Biggest Food Company
shorts.covers: Henri Nestlé's infant cereal in 1867, the merger with the Anglo-Swiss Condensed Milk Company, Nescafé, KitKat and Nespresso, and the controversies along the way.
shorts.subject: Nestlé
shorts.source: Nestlé official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Nestlé: From Baby Food to Food Giant
script.description: A chemist in a small Swiss town mixed milk, flour and sugar to feed babies who could not be breastfed. That recipe grew into the biggest food company in the world.

shorts.title: Zomato: From Scanned Menus to Food Delivery
shorts.covers: Deepinder Goyal scanning restaurant menus at his Delhi office in 2008, the restaurant listing site, the move into delivery, and the public listing in 2021.
shorts.subject: Zomato
shorts.source: Zomato official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Zomato: From Scanned Menus to Delivery
script.description: Two office workers in Delhi watched colleagues queue to read a pile of paper menus. They scanned them, put them online, and built one of India's biggest food delivery companies.

shorts.title: Grab: The Taxi App Two Classmates Built for South-East Asia
shorts.covers: Anthony Tan and Tan Hooi Ling's Harvard business plan, safer taxis in Kuala Lumpur, beating Uber in the region, and growing into payments and food delivery.
shorts.subject: Grab Holdings
shorts.source: Grab Holdings official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Grab: The Taxi App Built for South-East Asia
script.description: Two business school classmates wanted taxis in Malaysia to be safer. Their app beat Uber in South-East Asia and became the region's everyday app for rides, food and payments.

shorts.title: KFC: The Colonel Who Started Again at Sixty-Five
shorts.covers: Harland Sanders frying chicken at a roadside petrol station, his secret blend, selling franchises from the back of his car in old age, and how the brand spread across the globe.
shorts.subject: KFC
shorts.source: KFC official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: KFC: The Colonel Who Started Again at 65
script.description: At sixty-five, Harland Sanders lost his restaurant and had little more than a pension cheque. So he loaded a pressure cooker into his car and drove across America, selling his chicken recipe one kitchen at a time.

shorts.title: H&M: The Swedish Store That Made Fashion Cheap
shorts.covers: Erling Persson opening a women's clothing shop in Västerås in 1947 after seeing American retail, low prices on high volumes, and the designer collaborations that drew queues.
shorts.subject: H&M
shorts.source: H&M official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: H&M: The Swedish Shop for Cheap Fashion
script.description: A Swedish shopkeeper saw how American stores sold clothes in huge numbers at low prices. He opened one small shop called Hennes, meaning hers, and it grew into one of the world's biggest fashion chains.

shorts.title: Facebook: From a Dorm Room to Three Billion Users
shorts.covers: Mark Zuckerberg's Harvard network in 2004, the spread to other campuses, the News Feed, buying Instagram and WhatsApp, and the rename to Meta.
shorts.subject: Facebook Meta
shorts.source: Facebook Meta official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Facebook: From a Dorm Room to Billions
script.description: In 2004 a nineteen-year-old student built a website for his university friends. It spread to every campus in America, then the world, and three billion people now use it every month.

shorts.title: Stripe: Two Irish Brothers Who Fixed Online Payments
shorts.covers: Patrick and John Collison from rural Tipperary, seven lines of code to accept payments, winning over developers, and building the plumbing behind much of internet commerce.
shorts.subject: Stripe
shorts.source: Stripe official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Stripe: Two Brothers Fix Online Payments
script.description: Taking payments online once meant weeks of paperwork. Two brothers from a small village in Ireland made it take seven lines of code, and now trillions of dollars a year flow through their company.

shorts.title: Tesla: The Electric Car Startup Everyone Said Would Fail
shorts.covers: Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning founding Tesla in 2003, Elon Musk's investment, the Roadster, near-bankruptcy, the Model 3 production struggle, and becoming the most valuable carmaker.
shorts.subject: Tesla
shorts.source: Tesla official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Tesla: The Car Startup Expected to Fail
script.description: Two engineers believed electric cars could be fast and fun. Tesla nearly went bankrupt in 2008 and again during the Model 3, then became the most valuable car company in the world.

shorts.title: Barbie: The Doll That Made Mattel
shorts.covers: Ruth and Elliot Handler starting Mattel in a garage, Ruth seeing her daughter play with paper dolls, the launch of Barbie in 1959, and the doll's many reinventions.
shorts.subject: Mattel Barbie
shorts.source: Mattel Barbie official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Barbie: The Doll That Made Mattel
script.description: A mother watched her daughter play with paper dolls and pretend they were grown women. The company's men said no mother would buy such a doll. Barbie has since sold over a billion.

shorts.title: Levi's: The Gold Rush Trousers That Became Jeans
shorts.covers: Levi Strauss selling dry goods in San Francisco, tailor Jacob Davis's riveted work trousers, the patent of 1873, and denim's journey from miners to fashion.
shorts.subject: Levi Strauss
shorts.source: Levi Strauss official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Levi's: Gold Rush Trousers That Became Jeans
script.description: A tailor in Nevada put metal rivets in a working man's trousers so they would stop tearing. He needed a partner to pay for the patent, and wrote to the cloth seller Levi Strauss.

shorts.title: Heineken: The Brewery Bought by a 22-Year-Old
shorts.covers: Gerard Adriaan Heineken buying an Amsterdam brewery in 1864, the special yeast, export to America after Prohibition, and Freddy Heineken's marketing genius.
shorts.subject: Heineken
shorts.source: Heineken official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Heineken: The Brewery Bought by a 22-Year-Old
script.description: In 1864, a young man in Amsterdam persuaded his mother to buy the city's biggest brewery. His family turned it into one of the most famous beers in the world.

shorts.title: Paytm: The Mobile Wallet That Rode Demonetisation
shorts.covers: Vijay Shekhar Sharma from a small town in Uttar Pradesh, phone recharges, the digital wallet, the cash ban of 2016 that sent users soaring, and the regulatory troubles that followed.
shorts.subject: Paytm
shorts.source: Paytm official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Paytm: The Wallet That Rode Demonetisation
script.description: One night in 2016, India cancelled most of its banknotes. A phone payment app run by a teacher's son from a small town was ready, and millions signed up within weeks.

shorts.title: Shopee: The Gaming Company That Became an Online Shop
shorts.covers: Forrest Li founding Garena in Singapore to publish games, the hit Free Fire, and using game profits to build the shopping app Shopee across the region.
shorts.subject: Sea Limited Shopee
shorts.source: Sea Limited Shopee official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Shopee: The Game Company That Built a Shop
script.description: A businessman in Singapore built a games company, then used the money from its hit games to launch a shopping app. Shopee became the biggest online marketplace in South-East Asia.

shorts.title: Domino's: The Pizza Chain That Sold Speed
shorts.covers: Two brothers buying one pizzeria in Michigan in 1960, the bet on delivery, the famous thirty-minute promise, and the later reinvention as a technology company that happens to make pizza.
shorts.subject: Domino's Pizza
shorts.source: Domino's Pizza official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Domino's: The Pizza Chain That Sold Speed
script.description: Two brothers bought one struggling pizza shop in Michigan with borrowed money. One of them swapped his half for a Volkswagen Beetle. The other built the biggest pizza company in the world.

shorts.title: Costco: The Warehouse That Charges You to Shop
shorts.covers: Jim Sinegal and Jeffrey Brotman opening a Seattle warehouse in 1983, the membership-fee model, tiny margins, the hot dog price that never changes, and fierce customer loyalty.
shorts.subject: Costco
shorts.source: Costco official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Costco: The Shop That Charges You to Enter
script.description: Costco makes customers pay a yearly fee just to walk in, sells fewer products than a supermarket, and has kept its hot dog at the same price since 1985. Millions of people love it.

shorts.title: Nvidia: The Graphics Card Maker That Powered a Revolution
shorts.covers: Three engineers meeting at a Denny's diner in 1993, chips for video games, the CUDA bet that let graphics chips do general computing, and becoming one of the world's most valuable companies.
shorts.subject: Nvidia
shorts.source: Nvidia official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Nvidia: The Graphics Chip Maker Behind AI
script.description: Three engineers met in a roadside diner in 1993 to plan a company making graphics chips for video games. Those chips turned out to be exactly what modern artificial intelligence needed.

shorts.title: Duolingo: The Green Owl That Made Language Learning a Game
shorts.covers: Luis von Ahn, the inventor of CAPTCHA, wanting free education for all, the game-like lessons and streaks, and the mascot that became an internet celebrity.
shorts.subject: Duolingo
shorts.source: Duolingo official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Duolingo: The Owl That Made Learning a Game
script.description: A professor from Guatemala knew how much it cost poor people to learn English. He built a free app that turned language lessons into a game, starring a green owl that will not leave you alone.

shorts.title: Harley-Davidson: The Motorbike Built in a Backyard Shed
shorts.covers: William Harley and the Davidson brothers in a Milwaukee shed in 1903, military orders in two world wars, nearly collapsing in the 1980s, and the loyal owners who saved it.
shorts.subject: Harley-Davidson
shorts.source: Harley-Davidson official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Harley-Davidson: The Bike Built in a Shed
script.description: Two young men in Milwaukee built a motorised bicycle in a small wooden shed in 1903. Harley-Davidson survived wars, Japanese rivals and near ruin, saved in the end by the people who rode them.

shorts.title: Hasbro: From Pencil Cases to Monopoly and Transformers
shorts.covers: The Hassenfeld brothers selling textile remnants in Rhode Island, pencil boxes, Mr Potato Head, G.I. Joe, and buying Milton Bradley and Parker Brothers.
shorts.subject: Hasbro
shorts.source: Hasbro official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Hasbro: From Pencil Cases to Monopoly
script.description: Three immigrant brothers in America sold leftover cloth, then pencil cases, then toys. Their company sold the first toy ever advertised on television, and now makes Monopoly, Nerf and Transformers.

shorts.title: Ray-Ban: The Glasses Made for Pilots
shorts.covers: Bausch & Lomb's anti-glare lenses for US airmen in the 1930s, the Aviator and Wayfarer, film stardom, and the Italian company Luxottica that bought the brand.
shorts.subject: Luxottica Ray-Ban
shorts.source: Luxottica Ray-Ban official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Ray-Ban: The Glasses Made for Pilots
script.description: American pilots in the 1920s and 30s were suffering from headaches and sore eyes caused by the glare of the sky. An eyewear company made them special green lenses, and Ray-Ban was born.

shorts.title: Philips: The Light Bulb Factory That Lit Up Europe
shorts.covers: Gerard and Anton Philips making bulbs in Eindhoven in 1891, radios, the compact cassette and the CD, and the shift into health technology.
shorts.subject: Philips
shorts.source: Philips official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Philips: The Bulb Factory That Lit Up Europe
script.description: A father and son bought an empty factory in a small Dutch town to make light bulbs. A younger brother who loved selling joined them, and the company grew into Philips, maker of the cassette tape and the CD.

shorts.title: Nykaa: The Banker Who Started Again at Fifty
shorts.covers: Falguni Nayar leaving investment banking to sell beauty products online in 2012, building trust in a new market, and becoming one of India's richest self-made women.
shorts.subject: Nykaa
shorts.source: Nykaa official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Nykaa: The Banker Who Started Again at Fifty
script.description: After nearly twenty years as a top investment banker, Falguni Nayar left at the age of forty-nine to sell beauty products online. Her company Nykaa made her one of the richest women in India.

shorts.title: Jollibee: The Ice Cream Parlour That Beat McDonald's
shorts.covers: Tony Tan Caktiong's ice cream shop in Manila in 1975, adding hot food, sweet spaghetti and Chickenjoy for Filipino tastes, and winning its home market against global chains.
shorts.subject: Jollibee
shorts.source: Jollibee official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Jollibee: The Bee That Beat McDonald's
script.description: A young man in Manila opened an ice cream shop with his family. Customers wanted hot food, so he added burgers, then sweet spaghetti and crispy chicken, and built the restaurant that beats McDonald's in the Philippines.

shorts.title: Nutella: The Chocolate Spread Born from a Shortage
shorts.covers: Pietro Ferrero stretching scarce cocoa with hazelnuts in post-war Italy, the jar that became Nutella, and how one family built Kinder, Ferrero Rocher and Tic Tac while staying private.
shorts.subject: Ferrero
shorts.source: Ferrero official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Nutella: The Spread Born from a Shortage
script.description: After the Second World War, chocolate was scarce in Italy. A pastry maker stretched it with local hazelnuts, and his family turned that recipe into Nutella, Kinder and Ferrero Rocher.

shorts.title: Aldi: Two Brothers, One Shop, Two Empires
shorts.covers: Karl and Theo Albrecht taking over their mother's shop in Essen, the no-frills discount formula, the split into Aldi Nord and Aldi Süd, and their spread across Europe, the US and Australia.
shorts.subject: Aldi
shorts.source: Aldi official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Aldi: Two Brothers, One Shop, Two Empires
script.description: Two brothers took over their mother's small grocery shop in a German mining town after the war. They built a cheap, no-frills supermarket, then fell out and split the business in two.

shorts.title: Intel: The Company That Put a Brain in Every Computer
shorts.covers: Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore leaving Fairchild in 1968, memory chips, the first microprocessor, the 'Intel Inside' campaign and its long run at the heart of the PC.
shorts.subject: Intel
shorts.source: Intel official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Intel: The Brain Inside Every Computer
script.description: Two engineers left their company in 1968 to start Intel. Three years later, their team fitted a whole computer processor onto a single chip, and the age of personal computers began.

shorts.title: WhatsApp: The Messaging App With No Adverts
shorts.covers: Jan Koum and Brian Acton, two former Yahoo engineers, a status app that became a messenger, a tiny team serving hundreds of millions, and the 19 billion dollar sale to Facebook.
shorts.subject: WhatsApp
shorts.source: WhatsApp official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: WhatsApp: The Messaging App With No Adverts
script.description: A teenager who arrived in America from Ukraine with his mother and lived on food stamps built a messaging app with a friend. He signed its 19 billion dollar sale outside the welfare office where he once queued.

shorts.title: Ryanair: The Airline That Made Flying Cheap
shorts.covers: A small Irish airline flying from Waterford in 1985, nearly failing, copying Southwest's low-cost model, Michael O'Leary's no-frills approach, and becoming Europe's biggest carrier.
shorts.subject: Ryanair
shorts.source: Ryanair official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Ryanair: The Airline That Made Flying Cheap
script.description: A tiny Irish airline that began with one fifteen-seat plane was losing money fast. Then it copied a cheap American airline, cut everything it could, and became the biggest airline in Europe.

shorts.title: Disney: The Mouse That Built an Empire
shorts.covers: Walt and Roy Disney's cartoon studio, losing Oswald the rabbit, creating Mickey Mouse, the gamble on Snow White, Disneyland, and the modern company of parks and franchises.
shorts.subject: Walt Disney Company
shorts.source: Walt Disney Company official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Disney: The Mouse That Built an Empire
script.description: Walt Disney lost his first cartoon star to the man who paid for it. On the train home he dreamed up a mouse, and built one of the biggest entertainment companies in the world.

shorts.title: Dr. Martens: The Army Doctor's Boot That Joined the Punks
shorts.covers: A German doctor with an injured ankle designing an air-cushioned sole, the British Griggs family making the 1460 boot in 1960, and its adoption by workers, skinheads and punks.
shorts.subject: Dr. Martens
shorts.source: Dr. Martens official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Dr. Martens: The Doctor's Boot Punks Loved
script.description: A German army doctor hurt his ankle skiing and designed a boot with a soft air-cushioned sole. A family of English bootmakers added yellow stitching, and it became the boot of workers, then rebels.

shorts.title: ASML: The Dutch Company Every Chip Maker Needs
shorts.covers: A joint venture between Philips and ASM in a shed beside a factory in 1984, decades betting on lithography, and the extreme ultraviolet machines only it can make.
shorts.subject: ASML
shorts.source: ASML official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: ASML: The Machine Every Chip Maker Needs
script.description: Every advanced computer chip in the world is made on machines from one company in a small Dutch town. ASML began in a leaky shed in 1984, and spent decades building a machine others gave up on.

shorts.title: Wipro: The Vegetable Oil Company That Became an IT Giant
shorts.covers: Western India Vegetable Products in 1945, Azim Premji taking over at twenty-one after his father's death, the move into computers, and his record-setting philanthropy.
shorts.subject: Wipro
shorts.source: Wipro official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Wipro: From Cooking Oil to IT Giant
script.description: When his father died suddenly, a twenty-one-year-old student came home from America to run the family's cooking oil company. Azim Premji turned it into one of India's biggest technology firms.

shorts.title: Singapore Airlines: The Airline of a Country Without Domestic Flights
shorts.covers: The split from Malaysia-Singapore Airlines in 1972, the Singapore Girl, betting on service and new planes, and staying among the world's best-rated airlines.
shorts.subject: Singapore Airlines
shorts.source: Singapore Airlines official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Singapore Airlines: Nowhere to Fly at Home
script.description: Singapore is so small that it has no domestic flights, so every journey its airline makes is against the world's best. It decided to win on service, and became one of the best-rated airlines on Earth.

shorts.title: Heinz: The Ketchup That Promised Purity
shorts.covers: Henry John Heinz bottling horseradish in clear glass, the '57 varieties' slogan, his campaign for food safety laws, and how ketchup became the brand's global calling card.
shorts.subject: Heinz
shorts.source: Heinz official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Heinz: The Ketchup That Promised Purity
script.description: Other food sellers hid cheap fillers in dark bottles. A young man in Pittsburgh put his horseradish in clear glass so customers could see what they were buying, and built the most famous ketchup in the world.

shorts.title: Primark: Low Prices Without a Website
shorts.covers: Arthur Ryan opening the first Penneys in Dublin in 1969, the move into Britain under the Primark name, the bargain-fashion formula and the choice to stay mostly offline.
shorts.subject: Primark
shorts.source: Primark official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Primark: Low Prices Without a Website
script.description: An Irish businessman opened one cheap clothing shop in Dublin in 1969. Primark grew across Europe and America selling fashion at rock-bottom prices, almost without selling online at all.

shorts.title: Oracle: The Database Built From a CIA Project Name
shorts.covers: Larry Ellison and two partners reading a research paper on relational databases, the first commercial SQL product named after a CIA project, aggressive selling, and growth into a business software giant.
shorts.subject: Oracle
shorts.source: Oracle official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Oracle: A Database Named After a CIA Project
script.description: A college dropout read a research paper that a giant computer company was ignoring, and built a database from it. He named it after a CIA project he had worked on, and Oracle became a software giant.

shorts.title: Instagram: The Photo App Sold for a Billion With Thirteen Staff
shorts.covers: Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger dropping a check-in app called Burbn, filters for phone photos, a million users in two months, and the sale to Facebook in 2012.
shorts.subject: Instagram
shorts.source: Instagram official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Instagram: A Billion Dollars, Thirteen Staff
script.description: Two founders gave up on a complicated check-in app and kept only the part people used: sharing photos. Eighteen months later, Facebook paid a billion dollars for their company of thirteen people.

shorts.title: Southwest: The Airline Sketched on a Napkin
shorts.covers: Herb Kelleher and Rollin King drawing a triangle of Texas cities, years of legal fights to take off, quick turnarounds, one plane type, and decades of profits in a hard industry.
shorts.subject: Southwest Airlines
shorts.source: Southwest Airlines official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Southwest: The Airline Sketched on a Napkin
script.description: Two men drew a triangle between three Texas cities on a napkin. Big airlines fought them in court for years before their first flight, and Southwest became the most copied airline in the world.

shorts.title: Marvel: The Comic Book Company That Went Bankrupt, Then Ruled Cinema
shorts.covers: Timely Comics in 1939, Stan Lee and Jack Kirby's heroes of the 1960s, bankruptcy in 1996, the risky film studio, Iron Man, and the sale to Disney.
shorts.subject: Marvel Entertainment
shorts.source: Marvel Entertainment official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Marvel: From Bankruptcy to Ruling Cinema
script.description: Marvel's comic book heroes had flaws and money worries, and readers loved them. Then the company went bankrupt, and bet its own characters on a loan to make films itself.

shorts.title: Patagonia: The Company That Told You Not to Buy Its Jacket
shorts.covers: Yvon Chouinard forging climbing pitons, moving into clothing, the 'Don't Buy This Jacket' advert, and giving the company away to fight climate change.
shorts.subject: Patagonia
shorts.source: Patagonia official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Patagonia: Don't Buy This Jacket
script.description: A climber who made his own climbing gear in a backyard forge built an outdoor clothing company that told customers to buy less. Then he gave the whole company away to fight climate change.

shorts.title: Maersk: The Shipping Company That Moves the World's Goods
shorts.covers: A Danish captain and his son starting a steamship company in 1904, the shift to container ships, and growing into one of the largest shipping lines on earth.
shorts.subject: Maersk
shorts.source: Maersk official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Maersk: The Ships That Move the World
script.description: A Danish sea captain and his son bought one second-hand steamship in 1904. Their family company grew into one of the biggest container shipping lines on Earth, carrying the goods in your home.

shorts.title: HDFC Bank: The Bank That Was Built to Be Boring
shorts.covers: HDFC starting in housing finance in 1977, Aditya Puri building a new private bank from 1994, careful lending, and growing into India's largest private bank.
shorts.subject: HDFC Bank
shorts.source: HDFC Bank official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: HDFC Bank: Built on Purpose to Be Boring
script.description: A banker who was sixty-six years old started India's first home loan company. His company then built a bank that grew by being careful, and became India's biggest private bank.

shorts.title: M-Pesa: Money Sent by Text Message
shorts.covers: A Kenyan mobile network and a British aid-funded trial in 2007, people sending money from basic phones, and how it reshaped banking for millions.
shorts.subject: Safaricom M-Pesa
shorts.source: Safaricom M-Pesa official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: M-Pesa: Money Sent by Text Message
script.description: In Kenya, most people had no bank account, and sending money home meant trusting a bus driver with cash. A phone company tested a simple text message service, and changed how a whole country handles money.

shorts.title: Kellogg's: The Breakfast Born in a Health Sanitarium
shorts.covers: Two brothers at a Michigan health resort, the accidental flake, the bitter split over adding sugar, and the advertising that turned cereal into the default morning meal.
shorts.subject: Kellogg's
shorts.source: Kellogg's official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Kellogg's: Breakfast Born in a Health Spa
script.description: Two brothers at a Michigan health resort made flakes of grain by accident. One wanted to keep them plain and healthy. The other wanted to add sugar and sell them to everyone, and their fight lasted for years.

shorts.title: Sephora: The Store That Let You Touch the Make-Up
shorts.covers: Dominique Mandonnaud's open-sell perfume shops in France, the Sephora name, joining LVMH, and how letting customers test everything changed beauty retail.
shorts.subject: Sephora
shorts.source: Sephora official company history, annual reports and reputable business journalism

script.title: Sephora: The Shop That Let You Try Anything
script.description: In most perfume shops, the products sat locked behind a counter with a salesperson guarding them. A Frenchman opened a shop where customers could pick up and try anything they liked, and built Sephora.
